idiom_name: CoroutineCrudRepository / JpaRepository interface with suspend query methods
implementation_notes: Spring Data JPA generates the implementation for a Kotlin interface extending CoroutineCrudRepository<T, ID> (or JpaRepository); suspend query methods run on the caller's coroutine dispatcher without blocking the thread, and derived names plus @Query work as in Java. Shared method sets go into a @NoRepositoryBean base interface, and Kotlin collection return types (List) are preferred over Iterable for clarity. The classic hand-written structure disappears; keep the interface in the domain module so the generated proxy stays an implementation detail.
pitfalls: Suspend repository calls must run inside a coroutine scope and a transaction boundary (@Transactional / withContext); a blocking JDBC call inside a suspend function stalls the dispatcher instead of blocking a thread pool.
Coroutine support needs the coroutine extension dependency; without it the repository methods are plain blocking calls and the suspend modifier is a lie.
Repository interfaces with many derived queries are parsed at start-up and can dominate boot time in large applications.

variants.name: JetBrains Exposed table object and DSL inside a transaction block
variants.idiom_name: Exposed Table object + select/insert DSL inside transaction { }
variants.implementation_notes: JetBrains Exposed gives a typed SQL DSL: one Table object per table, Invoices.selectAll().where { ... } as the collection-like query surface inside transaction { }, and an optional DAO layer (EntityClass/Entity) for identity-based persistence. The repository stays hand-written but thin, holding the Database and mapping rows to domain objects; choose it for Kotlin-first stacks without JPA, or when compile-checked column references and explicit SQL matter more than ORM convenience.
pitfalls: Nested transaction { } blocks reuse the outer transaction and do not commit independently, which surprises code that expects its own transaction.
DAO entities are bound to the transaction that loaded them: passing them outside gives detached or re-loaded state, so prefer the DSL with plain data classes for the domain.
Exposed's DSL is SQL-shaped: complex dynamic predicates still need explicit construction, so keep ad-hoc reporting queries out of the repository interface.
